newsitem.title: USA: Apple to unveil new laptop, PCs Monday.
newsitem.headline: Apple to unveil new laptop, PCs Monday.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc. said Thursday it will unveil on Monday a new PowerBook laptop, updated Power Macintosh desktop computers, a new digital camera and a laptop for kids.

The products are part of Apple's three-year plan to get sales going again after losing out in the past year to rivals that rolled out hordes of personal computers based on Microsoft Corp.'s Windows 95.

Apple said its new PowerBook 3400 is one of the fastest laptops ever built. The 3400 -- with prices ranging from $4,500 to $6,500 -- features the speedy PowerPC 603e microprocessor, a built-in modem and four-speaker sound.

Apple also will unveil updated models in its Power Macintosh computers. With prices ranging from $1,700 to $4,700, the machines are aimed at business users and desktop publishers, Apple said. The Power Macintosh 9600/200 MP uses two PowerPC microprocessors to handle complex graphics editing tasks.

For the education market, Apple will introduce the eMate 300, a laptop in a rugged plastic casing designed for grade school students. Based on Apple's handheld Newton computer, the eMate will be sold directly to schools starting at $749.
The company also will show the QuickTake 200, a $600 digital camera that records photographs in computer memory.
All the new products will be available by spring, Apple said. Apple's stock rose 37.5 cents to $16.125 on Nasdaq.
